newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BIL's Matthew sees better return from Air NZ.
newsitem.headline: BIL's Matthew sees better return from Air NZ.

text.p: Brierley Investments Ltd Chairman Bob Matthew said on Wednesday he expected BIL's associate, Air New Zealand, to return to more acceptable levels from the 1998 year onwards.

"While the negative influences on the first half outcome of NZ$78 million, 43 percent down on the previous year, will also impact on the full year result, the longer term outlook is encouraging," Matthew, who also chairs Air NZ, told the New Zealand Investment Conference.
Air NZ now has a half share in Australia's Ansett and recently signed a strategic alliance with United Airlines.

"Given the strategic initiatives referred to earlier, the wide ranging cost reduction programmes under way at both Ansett and Air New Zealand, declining fuel prices and the modest capacity expanison planned for the next two years or so, a return to more acceptable levels of profitability is expected from the 1998 year onwards," Matthew said.
Commenting on BIL's investment in British hotels group Thistle, Matthew said the outlook was positive.

"The ongoing substantial upgrading of the group's hotels, the expansion of the Thistle Four Star brand, the organic growth of up to 2,000 additional rooms, the progressive switching towards commercial and higher spend leisure business and a buoyant domestic U.K. economy together augur well for Thistle's performance and, thereby, the value value of BIL's residual investment," Matthew said.
